Supportive in vitro transport studies
To assess the potential involvement of transporters in the distribution and elimination of GuHong compounds, the cellular uptake of these compounds at a concentration of 20 μmol/L was investigated in HEK-293 cells that were transiently transfected with human OAT1, OAT2, OAT3, OATP1B1, and OATP1B3 and rat Oatp1b2 and Oat2. The transporter expression plasmid was introduced into the HEK-293 cells using Lipofectamine 2000 (Invitrogen, Carlsbad, CA, USA). Cell culture and transport studies were performed as previously described[46–47]. Differential uptake between transfected cells (TC) and mock cells (MC) was defined as the net transport ratio (Transport /Transport ). A net transport ratio >3 indicated that the test compound was a substrate of the transporter. Before use, the transfected cells were functionally characterized by measuring the uptake of para-aminohippuric acid, prostaglandin $\mathrm { F } _ { 2 a } ,$ estrone-3-sulfate, and estradiol-17-β-D-glucuronide for OAT1, OAT2/Oat2, OAT3, and OATP1B1/OATP1B3/Oatp1b2, respectively.The GuHong compounds were assessed for their inhibition of human OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3, OCT2, MATE1, and MATE2K. Probe substrates for OATP1B1/OATP1B3, OAT1, OAT3, and OCT2/ MATE1/MATE2K were estradiol-17-β-D-glucuronide, para-aminohippuric acid, estrone-3-sulfate, and tetraethylammonium (10 μmol/L for all), respectively. The initial screening for inhibitory activity was conducted at the concentrations used in the enzyme inhibition study for the test compounds. When >50% inhibition was demonstrated in the initial screening test, the $\mathrm { I C } _ { 5 0 }$ was determined for the transporters.Inside-out membrane vesicles expressing human MDR1, MRP2, BCRP, or BSEP, or rat Mrp2, Bcrp, or Bsep were tested with GuHong compounds, each at 20 µmol/L, using a rapid filtration method as described previously[47]. ATP was used as the energy source to transport the test compounds across the vesicle membrane, and AMP was used as a negative control. ATPdependent transport was defined as the net transport ratio (Transpor $\cdot _ { \mathrm { A T p } } / \mathrm { T r a n s p o r t } _ { \mathrm { A M P } }$ ratio). A net transport ratio >3 indicated that the test compound was a substrate of the transporter. The vesicles were functionally characterized using ginsenoside $\mathrm { R g } _ { \mathrm { 1 } } \mathrm { : }$ , estradiol-17β-Dglucuronide, methotrexate, and taurocholic acid as a substrate for MDR1, MRP2/Mrp2, BCRP/Bcrp, and BSEP/Bsep, respectively.The ability of the GuHong compounds to inhibit human MDR1 and BCRP was assessed. Probe substrates for MDR1 and BCRP were ginsenoside $\mathrm { R g } _ { 1 }$ and methotrexate (10 μmol/L for both), respectively. The initial screening for inhibitory activity was conducted at the concentrations used in the enzyme inhibition study for the test compounds. When ${ > } 5 0 \%$ inhibition was demonstrated in the initial screening test, the $\mathrm { I C } _ { 5 0 }$ was determined for the transporters.
